filename: Scale-Dependent Drivers of Air-Sea CO2 Flux Variability.pdf
title: Scale-Dependent Drivers of Air-Sea CO2 Flux Variability
code_availability: Model code and platform-independent instructions for running the ECCO-Darwin simulations described in this study are available at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10627664 and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13259496.
testbed_rationale: The study conducts numerical sensitivity runs with the ECCO-Darwin ocean model to quantify drivers of air-sea CO2 flux variability; it does not evaluate, propose, or format benchmarks for ML parameterizations or emulators.
pain_points: Separating internal climate variability from forced variability in observational and multi-model ensembles
Multi-model ensemble averaging dampens internal variability inherent to individual models, artificially amplifying common atmospheric forcing signals
High amplitude of localized climate-driven variability obscures the detection of emerging signals from slowing atmospheric CO2 growth rates without denser observing networks
extraction_notes: The paper does not apply or develop ML algorithms; it analyzes a set of physical-biogeochemical GCM simulations funded in part by NSF LEAP STC (Award 2019625).
